cards.title: When does truth-table reconstruction preserve an intuitionistic connective?
cards.formal: For every n≥1 and every propositional formula F(p₁,…,pₙ) built from ∧, ∨, → and ¬, suppose that each disjunction subformula P∨Q has both P and Q free of → and ¬, each implication subformula P→Q has P free of → and ¬, and each negation subformula ¬P has P free of → and ¬. Let c_F be a fresh n-ary connective with the constructive truth-table natural-deduction rules below, derived from the classical Boolean truth table of F. Must c_F(A₁,…,Aₙ) and F(A₁,…,Aₙ) be interderivable in intuitionistic logic with those rules, for every substitution of formulas A₁,…,Aₙ? The syntactic restriction is checked on the template F before substitution.
cards.why: Would give a syntactic guarantee that automatic proof-rule generation preserves a defined connective’s intuitionistic meaning, clarifying the expressive limits of truth-table natural deduction.
cards.status_note: Read the complete rule generator and conjecture in the published paper and searched later work on truth-table natural deduction through 12 September 2026. cards.definitions: Formulas are finite syntax trees over propositional variables and the listed connectives; repeated variables are allowed. The restriction “free of → and ¬” means that only variables, ∧ and ∨ occur in that subformula. The Boolean truth table t_F:{0,1}ⁿ→{0,1} evaluates ∧ as conjunction, ∨ as disjunction, → as material implication and ¬ as complement. For a substitution A=(A₁,…,Aₙ), write Φ=c_F(A). Derivations are finite intuitionistic natural-deduction derivations with the usual assumption, conjunction, disjunction, implication and negation rules, including falsity elimination; ¬B has its usual intuitionistic meaning B→⊥. Add the following rule schemata, with Γ a finite context and D any formula. For each row r with t_F(r)=0, from Γ⊢Φ, all premises Γ⊢Aᵢ with rᵢ=1, and all premises Γ,Aⱼ⊢D with rⱼ=0, infer Γ⊢D, discharging the indicated extra assumptions. For each row r with t_F(r)=1, from all Γ⊢Aᵢ with rᵢ=1 and all Γ,Aⱼ⊢Φ with rⱼ=0, infer Γ⊢Φ, again discharging the indicated assumptions. An empty family of premises contributes no requirement. Rule instances may use arbitrary formulas in the extended language; no excluded-middle or classical introduction rule is added. Interderivable means that both Φ⊢F(A) and F(A)⊢Φ have such derivations. This is an exact syntactic equivalence claim with no computational-resource or probability bound.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove both derivability directions for every qualifying formula template and every substitution, or refute the universal statement with a qualifying template for which at least one direction is not derivable in the specified calculus. A mismatch for a template violating the syntactic condition is not a counterexample; classical equivalence alone is insufficient.

cards.title: An unrestricted exact wait-free FIFO queue in O(log n) steps
cards.formal: Is there a deterministic implementation of an exact, linearizable FIFO queue for n≥2 asynchronous processes such that every enqueue and dequeue finishes within C log₂(n+1) of its own steps, for one constant C independent of the execution, the queue length and n, with every process allowed to perform either operation? The guarantee is worst-case for each operation under arbitrary scheduling and crashes. The intended bound on one memory word, which affects whether this is still open, is missing from the source’s system model.
cards.why: Tests whether exact ordering and individual progress can coexist with logarithmic worst-case operation latency under unrestricted concurrent access.
cards.status_note: Checked the full OPODIS 2022 and PODC 2023 papers and searched subsequent work through 12 September 2026. No matching ordinary-word, queue-length-independent O(log n) worst-case result was located. The original question still needs a precise word/cost convention before openness can be certified.

progress.text: The source achieves O(log n) enqueue and O(k log n) dequeue steps for k dequeuers and asks for logarithmic worst-case complexity without that restriction.
The PODC follow-up achieves O(log n) enqueues and O(log² n+log q) dequeues using single-word CAS; its introduction also identifies the wide-word universal-construction caveat.

cards.definitions: There are n sequential processes with distinct identifiers, using shared memory; a process can stop permanently at any time. A process invokes a new queue operation only after its previous one returns. Initially the queue is empty. Enqueue(v) appends a value v; Dequeue() removes and returns the earliest remaining value, or returns a distinguished EMPTY value if none remains. Linearizability means that completed operations, together with any pending operations needed to complete the history, admit a legal sequential FIFO ordering respecting real-time precedence: an operation returning before another is invoked must come first. Wait-freedom requires each operation of a process that continues taking steps to finish after boundedly many of that process’s steps, regardless of the others. The source counts atomic base-object accesses and high-level invocation/response events. Base primitives include atomic read/write, fetch-and-increment (return the old integer and add one), and compare-and-swap (replace a value only if it equals the supplied expected value). Restricted max-register uses in the source are implemented by constantly many CAS primitives; they do not provide arbitrary uncharged computation. Shared memory may grow with the execution. The requested step bound must not depend on the current queue length q or the number of earlier operations. The source has not specified the bit capacity of a primitive-accessible word or how local computation is charged.
cards.answer_criterion: Fix the intended memory-word and cost convention, then prove or refute existence of one exact wait-free linearizable implementation with the stated per-operation worst-case bound. A correct construction must handle arbitrary well-formed histories with all n processes both enqueuing and dequeuing. An amortized or expected bound, a bound depending on q, a fixed limit on dequeuers, or relaxed multiplicity semantics does not establish this target.

cards.title: Centers of aperiodicity in three-dimensional shifts of finite type
cards.formal: Does every shift of finite type X⊆Σ^{ℤ³} that contains at least one aperiodic configuration contain an aperiodic configuration with the “center of aperiodicity” property proposed by Callard and Hellouin de Menibus? The source describes concentric zones witnessing broken periods at distances controlled by the period vector’s length, the alphabet size and the largest forbidden-pattern size. It does not state the precise zone/radius requirement. The desired configuration may differ from the initially given one; the conjecture is not a claim about every aperiodic configuration or its orbit closure.
cards.why: Would identify a structural constraint on three-dimensional tiling systems and clarify why detecting nonperiodic behavior may differ so sharply between dimensions.

cards.definitions: Σ is a finite nonempty alphabet. A configuration is a map x:ℤ³→Σ. A finite pattern assigns symbols to a finite set of lattice sites. Given a finite list F of forbidden patterns, the shift of finite type X consists of all configurations containing no translate of any pattern in F. Its presentation is finite even though its configurations are infinite. A vector v∈ℤ³ is a period of x if x(u)=x(u+v) for every u∈ℤ³. The configuration is aperiodic if zero is its only period; a witness breaking v≠0 is a site u with x(u)≠x(u+v). Translating a configuration shifts all its coordinates. Its orbit closure consists of limits of such translates, where convergence means eventual agreement on each finite set of sites. A center is intended to organize witnesses for different period lengths in bounded concentric regions around one lattice location. The source’s unspecified radius and region conventions are part of the missing mathematical predicate, not established definitions.
cards.answer_criterion: Recover the quantitative and effective center predicate intended by the source, then prove it for every three-dimensional SFT containing an aperiodic point, or exhibit an SFT that violates it while still containing an aperiodic point. Aperiodicity alone, a theorem only in two dimensions, or a center for one special SFT does not establish the universal structural claim. No result is required for the orbit closure of each prescribed aperiodic point.

cards.title: Exact Nash equilibria for infinite-horizon concurrent stochastic games
cards.area: Algorithmic game theory, mechanism design and fair division
cards.formal: Do all concurrent stochastic games in the infinite-horizon objective class intended by the MFCS 2022 survey admit an exact Nash equilibrium? The survey contrasts finite-horizon analysis with this existence question, but the excerpt and its cited reference do not determine a single common payoff, observation and equilibrium model. The quantifier “all” must therefore remain attached to a model still requiring specification; it is not a claim about every stochastic game with an arbitrary real-valued payoff.
cards.why: Exact equilibrium existence determines whether an infinite-duration multi-agent model has stable behavior at all, before verification can optimize or synthesize such behavior.

sentences: The question concerns stable strategic behavior in games with simultaneous actions and no fixed time horizon.
Exact Nash equilibrium forbids any profitable unilateral change of strategy.
Finite-horizon and approximate equilibrium results do not automatically imply exact infinite-horizon existence.
The survey and its underlying citation use different information conventions and discuss several payoff classes.
Those choices must be reconciled before this card can specify one universal existence theorem.

cards.definitions: The survey’s finite-state concurrent stochastic game has a finite set S of states, an initial state s₀, finitely many players i∈{1,…,m}, a finite nonempty action set Aᵢ(s) at each state, and a transition distribution δ(s,a₁,…,aₘ) on S. Players act simultaneously; the next state is drawn from this distribution. A behavioral strategy assigns a distribution on available actions to each finite observed history; players randomize independently. In Definition 10 the history includes past states and joint actions. There is no predetermined terminal time. Each player maximizes the expectation of a specified measurable payoff Xᵢ on infinite plays, under conditions ensuring the expectation is defined. A profile σ is an exact Nash equilibrium from s₀ if Eσ,s₀[Xᵢ]≥E(τᵢ,σ₋ᵢ),s₀[Xᵢ] for every player i and every admissible unilateral strategy τᵢ. An ε-equilibrium allows the right side to exceed the left by at most ε; existence for every ε>0 does not assert existence at ε=0. Requiring the equilibrium inequality from all states, or after every history, is an additional requirement. In the cited terminal-reward model, an absorbing terminal state carries each player’s reward and a nonterminating play pays zero; terminal-reachability rewards are restricted to {0,1}. These conventions describe the sources, not a recovered choice between their models.
cards.answer_criterion: After recovering the intended payoff, observation and equilibrium restrictions, prove that every game in that class has an exact equilibrium, or refute that universal statement by a game in the same class with no such equilibrium. An ε-equilibrium theorem, a finite-horizon theorem, or an undecidability result for a constrained equilibrium search task does not by itself settle that existence statement.

context_blocks.title: Finite state does not mean finite play
context_blocks.text: Even a game with finitely many states can continue forever. Payoffs may distinguish eventual termination from perpetual play, so the equilibrium question changes when an imposed time limit is removed.

context_blocks.title: The cited result is more specific than the excerpt
context_blocks.text: The 2014 paper proves undecidability of constrained equilibrium existence for three-player terminal-reachability games. It also proves undecidability of unconstrained existence for terminal rewards that may be negative. These are precise algorithmic statements, not a generic declaration that equilibrium existence is open.

context_blocks.title: Information affects deviations
context_blocks.text: The 2014 model observes only visited states, not the action profile producing a transition. The survey’s definition includes joint actions in histories. Existence and hardness results cannot be transferred between those strategy spaces without justification.

context_blocks.title: A narrower existence question remains in the cited conclusion
context_blocks.text: The 2014 conclusion explicitly retains the two-player nonnegative-terminal-reward existence question and discusses an earlier incorrect counterexample. This explains why the citation requires careful scoping; it does not select that restricted question on behalf of the survey.

context_blocks.title: Remaining formulation issue
context_blocks.text: The survey does not isolate one payoff family and player-count restriction for its brief infinite-horizon existence question. Its general CSG strategies observe states and joint actions, whereas reference [7] permits only state-history observation. The survey also focuses on equilibrium from every state, while the underlying existence discussion includes ordinary Nash equilibrium from an initial state. The intended objective class, observation convention and equilibrium requirement must be reconciled before one universal proposition can be certified. The continuous-state neuro-symbolic extension must not be substituted silently.

meta.status_scope: No claim of exhaustive open-status verification
methodology: Detailed cards have individually written statements, context, significance, and documented results. Source notes are unfinished research records and do not yet meet that standard. The legacy index is retained for traceability.
Open in the source means open at the date of that source. The build date, 10 September 2026, does not establish current open status. Old excerpts may omit conditions or subsequent results.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.

Textbook and survey questions are dated paraphrases; source locations, conjectures, research directions and caveats are preserved on the problem cards. These annotations do not establish current open status or change a later card review. New source drafts remain unassessed for importance. The reader contains the imported questions and external bibliographic references only; source files are not bundled.

Selection groups follow the agreed 10 large and 25 small categories. We aim for benchmarks of 100 and 500 problems, with a possible expansion to 1,000. All three use the same category order and the same ranking within each category. The respective prefixes are 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 problems per large/small category. The possible 1,000-problem expansion has 1000 assigned places and 0 reserved places. Each card records its category explicitly. These counts describe saved candidates; classification does not verify a statement or its current open status. Deleted records are absent from the catalogue and exports. Their stable IDs and reasons are retained to prevent reimport. Final quota selection and a comprehensive deduplication audit remain pending.

Importance ordering is an editorial assessment of foundational significance, breadth of consequences, and influence on other questions. Each assessed card gives a reason. The category-wide review also uses shared priority bands for questions of comparable scope; it does not claim that these ties have a scientifically meaningful internal order. Unassessed drafts share a provisional score of 50; their relative order is only an ID tie-break, not an importance judgment. The first 5/2 places in each large/small category are an explicit editorial focus selection balancing importance and topical diversity. Focus ordering does not alter importance scores; remaining candidates use score and ID order. The targets are 100 and 500 problems, with a possible expansion to 1,000. Top 100, Top 500 and the possible Top 1000 use the first 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 category places respectively, all from the same ranking. Category positions include all candidates and remain fixed when filtering. Publication date, source date, and card detail do not increase importance. Records marked resolved are placed after the remaining candidates, without changing their historical importance score. Importance review does not establish that a saved question is still open.

benchmark_selection.basis: Individual editorial review of saved titles, importance rationales, problem statements, source notes and working summaries. This is a review of importance and topical diversity, not a fresh verification of open status or completion of draft formulations. Importance scores are preserved.
